title: Henselian SNC neighborhoods with universal residual cover
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic a positive prime $p$. Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], and let $D=\bigcup_{a\in A}D_a$ be a reduced strict normal crossings boundary with finitely many components [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Fix $I\subseteq A$, put $Y_I=Y\setminus\bigcup_{a\notin I}D_a$, and give $S=(\bigcap_{i\in I}D_i)\cap Y_I$ its reduced structure. Empty intersections mean $Y$. There is an affine etale covering of $S$ by charts $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\to Y_I$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] on which the $D_i$ have global equations $t_i$; at every point where several $t_i$ vanish they are part of a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Write $J=(t_i)_{i\in I}$. The charts can be chosen with $S_V=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ nonempty and connected, and each $V$ regular, Noetherian and separated.

For each chart there is an affine ind-etale map $u:U=\operatorname{Spec}H\to V$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] with $S_U=\operatorname{Spec}(H/JH)$ nonempty and connected and a pro-etale covering $S_U\to S_V$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. More precisely, $S_U$ is the inverse limit of the pointed connected finite etale Galois covers of $S_V$ in [lem-sfb-pointed-finite-etale-limit-cover], and $(H,JH)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. The construction is obtained by henselizing $(B,J)$ and taking the filtered colimit of the finite etale algebras lifting this pointed cover system. There are compatible primitive roots $\zeta_n\in H$ for all $n>0$ prime to $p$, with $\zeta_m^{m/n}=\zeta_n$ for $n\mid m$ and $\zeta_n^a-\zeta_n^b$ a unit for distinct residues $a,b$ modulo $n$.

Throughout the following root constructions $n$ ranges over the positive integers prime to $p$, ordered by divisibility. Put $H_n=H[x_i\mid i\in I]/(x_i^n-t_i)_{i\in I}$, $H_\infty=\varinjlim_nH_n$ with the power transitions, $U^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}H[1/\prod_i t_i]$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}H_\infty$, and $T^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}H_\infty[1/\prod_i t_i]$. All $U,U^\circ,\operatorname{Spec}H_n,T,T^\circ$ are nonempty connected qcqs schemes. The finite and full parameter-root algebras over any strictly henselian regular Noetherian local ring of characteristic $p$ with a partial regular parameter system also have nonempty connected spectra and nonempty connected punctured spectra. Every $\operatorname{Spec}H_n[1/\prod_i t_i]\to U^\circ$ and every divisibility transition on these punctured levels is finite etale and surjective. Their inverse limit is a pro-etale covering $T^\circ\to U^\circ$. The family $S_U\to S$ covers $S$. The empty stratum has the empty family. On overlaps these constructions admit common refinements through a fixed geometric point of the stratum, and compatible pullback maps of the displayed rings and root systems (after choosing compatible roots of the units relating two labelled parameter equations). For $I=\varnothing$, $H_n=H_\infty=H$, $S_V=V$, and $U\to V$ is its pointed universal finite-etale limit cover.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian, so $Y$ and its open $Y_I$ are Noetherian. Let $P_a$ be the ideal of the component $D_a$, an integral regular closed subscheme of the boundary definition. Fix $y\in Y_I$, put $J_y=\{i\in I:y\in D_i\}$ and $\mathcal O=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, regular local of dimension $d$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. For $i\in J_y$, $\mathcal O/P_{i,y}=\mathcal O_{D_i,y}$ is regular local of dimension $d-1$ by the boundary dimension formula. The quotient-kernel theorem gives $P_{i,y}=(x_1,\ldots,x_c)$ for part of a regular system, and the regular-sequence theorem gives dimension $d-c$, so $c=1$: any generator $s_i$ of $P_{i,y}$ is a nonzerodivisor of the domain $\mathcal O$. The intersection ideal $I'=\sum_{i\in J_y}(s_i)$ has $\mathcal O/I'=\mathcal O_{C_{J_y},y}$ regular local of dimension $d-|J_y|$, so likewise $I'=(x_1,\ldots,x_{|J_y|})$ for part of a regular system. Each generating set expresses the other modulo $\mathfrak mI'\subseteq\mathfrak m^2$. So the classes of the $s_i$ span the same $|J_y|$-dimensional subspace of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ as the $x_j$; they are distinct and independent, and by Nakayama they extend to a regular system of parameters. As $P_i$ has finite type, a generator of $P_{i,y}$ generates $P_i$ on an affine open $W\ni y$ of $Y_I$ missing the $D_i$ with $i\notin J_y$. For $y\in S$, $J_y=I$, so every $D_i$ has a global equation $t_i$ on $W$. At each $y'\in W$ the $t_i$ vanishing at $y'$ generate the $P_{i,y'}$, so the same argument shows they are part of a regular system there. The ideal of $S\cap W$ is $J=(t_i)$, and $C_I$ is regular, hence reduced, so this is the reduced stratum. Open immersions are etale.

proof.text: The regular Noetherian schemes $Y_I$ and $S$ have disjoint open-and-closed integral components. Around each point $s\in S$, restrict to the ambient component through $s$ and remove from an affine chart all other components of its intersection with $S$. Take an affine open neighbourhood of $s$ inside that open. Its intersection $S_V$ with $S$ is a nonempty open of one integral component, hence is integral and connected: any two nonempty basic opens in a domain meet. Retain the functions $t_i$ by restriction. Then $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is regular, Noetherian, affine and separated, and $S_V=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$, $J=(t_i)$, is nonempty connected regular. Since $S$ is quasi-compact, finitely many such charts suffice. Fix a geometric point $s$ of each $S_V$.

source.place: VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p.118; agent choice of connected affine stratum charts

proof.text: Form the pair henselization $A=B^h$. Its construction is a small filtered colimit of etale $B$-algebras, $A/JA=B/J$, and $(A,JA)$ is henselian. As $B$ is Noetherian, $A$ is Noetherian. Reduction identifies idempotents of $A$ with those of $A/JA$: apply the henselian definition to the finite algebra $A$ itself. The latter ring is nonzero and has only idempotents $0,1$, because $S_V$ is nonempty connected. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is nonempty connected. Its affineness gives qcqs. The point $s$ maps to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by $A\to A/JA\to\Omega$.

source.place: Tags 0A02 (lemma-henselization), 0AGV (lemma-henselization-Noetherian-pair); idempotent definition of henselian pairs

proof.text: Apply the pointed finite-etale limit-cover theorem to the nonempty connected qcqs scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $s$. Write its small cofinal pointed connected finite etale Galois system as $\operatorname{Spec}C_\lambda\to X$ and put $H=\varinjlim_\lambda C_\lambda$. For the henselian pair $(A,JA)$ apply finite-etale lifting with the proper morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ equal to the identity. This identifies its finite-etale category, including morphisms and group actions, with that of $S_V$. Idempotent lifting shows that connected objects correspond to connected objects. Fibres at the same point $s$ agree. Thus this equivalence identifies the entire pointed connected Galois system with the one over $S_V$, not merely its objects. Quotienting the colimit by the finitely generated ideal $J$ gives $H/JH=\varinjlim_\lambda C_\lambda/JC_\lambda$: maps out of either ring are exactly compatible maps killing the $t_i$. Therefore $S_U=\operatorname{Spec}(H/JH)$ is precisely the pointed universal finite-etale limit of $S_V$. It is nonempty connected and is a pro-etale covering of $S_V$.

source.place: Tag 09ZS (lemma-gabber); agent assembly of the pointed cover and reduction, using the existing universal-cover node

proof.text: Each $C_\lambda$ is finite etale over the Noetherian ring $A$, hence Noetherian. Each is integral over $A$, and so is $H$: an element of $H$ comes from a finite stage and satisfies there a monic polynomial over $A$. Consequently $(C_\lambda,JC_\lambda)$ and $(H,JH)$ are henselian. Their marked ideals are contained in their Jacobson radicals. The map $B\to A$ is ind-etale by the henselization construction, and $A\to H$ is ind-etale by its finite-etale presentation. Stability under composition makes $B\to H$ ind-etale. Thus $U\to V$ is affine ind-etale, and all the specified henselian assertions hold.

source.place: Tags 09XK (lemma-integral-over-henselian-pair), 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), and 0A02; ind-etale stability

proof.text: The ring $B$ is regular Noetherian and $B\to A\to C_\lambda$ is ind-etale, by step 5 and since every etale map is ind-etale; ind-etale maps are weakly etale, hence flat. Let $\mathfrak p\subset B$ be prime and $F=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_BC_\lambda$. By base change $F$ is ind-etale, hence weakly etale, over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The weak-etale field theorem makes $F$ reduced and puts every element of $F$ in a finite etale, hence finite, $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-subalgebra. If $\mathfrak Q\subset F$ is prime, a nonzero element of the domain $F/\mathfrak Q$ satisfies a monic equation over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with nonzero constant term, so it is invertible. Thus every prime is maximal, each $F_\mathfrak Q$ is a reduced zero-dimensional local ring, and its maximal ideal, the nilradical, is zero. So $F_\mathfrak Q$ is a field, and $F$ (Noetherian, a localization of $C_\lambda/\mathfrak pC_\lambda$) is regular. Flat ascent gives regularity of the Noetherian ring $C_\lambda$. Now let $\mathfrak m\subset C_\lambda$ be maximal. It contains $JC_\lambda$ by the Jacobson conclusion of step 5, so $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m\cap B$ is a point of $S_V$. By step 1 the $t_i$ are part of a regular system of parameters of $B_\mathfrak p$. Then they form a $B_\mathfrak p$-regular sequence and $B_\mathfrak p/(t_i)$ is regular local. The local map $B_\mathfrak p\to R:=(C_\lambda)_\mathfrak m$ is flat. Tensoring the injective multiplications by $t_{j+1}$ on $B_\mathfrak p/(t_1,\ldots,t_j)$ with $R$ keeps them injective, and $R/(t_i)\neq0$ since all $t_i\in\mathfrak m$. So the $t_i$ form an $R$-regular sequence. The closed fibre $R/\mathfrak pR$ is a localization of $F$ at a prime, hence a field. The flat local map $B_\mathfrak p/(t_i)\to R/(t_i)$ has the same closed fibre, so the regular-fibre theorem makes $R/(t_i)$ regular local. Each $C_\lambda$ is nonempty connected by construction, so regularity and the Noetherian normal decomposition show that it is a domain.

source.place: Tag 031E (flat local map, regular base and regular closed fibre) and Tag 092Q (weakly etale over a field); agent application to the finite stages $C_\lambda$

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed geometric fibre field $\Omega$ for the point $s$. For each prime $q\ne p$, choose recursively primitive $q^a$-th roots in $\Omega$ whose $q$-th powers are the roots already chosen. Such a lift exists and is primitive: any $q$-th root of a primitive $q^a$-th root has order $q^{a+1}$. For different primes take products and, by the Chinese remainder theorem for the exponents, obtain primitive roots $\bar\zeta_n$ for all $(n,p)=1$, with $\bar\zeta_m^{m/n}=\bar\zeta_n$ whenever $n\mid m$. Equivalently these choices specify a generator at every level of the prime-to-$p$ Tate module.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, printed p.133, compatible roots for the parameter-root calculation; agent explicit compatible selection in the geometric fibre

proof.text: For $(n,p)=1$, the algebra $A[z]/(z^n-1)$ is finite free by monic division and etale: its derivative $nz^{n-1}$ is a unit, so its monic presentation is the standard-etale presentation. The universal-cover splitting over $\operatorname{Spec}H$, applied to this finite etale $X$-scheme, gives a section for each fibre root. Choose the section indexed by $\bar\zeta_n$, and denote its value by $\zeta_n\in H$. Naturality of that splitting for the power maps on root-of-unity schemes proves $\zeta_m^{m/n}=\zeta_n$. The same splitting identifies the finite etale group scheme $\mu_n$ over $H$ with the constant group on its geometric fibre. Distinct powers therefore remain distinct at every prime of $H$, so $\zeta_n^a-\zeta_n^b$ is in no maximal ideal and is a unit. In particular these are primitive roots in the stated strong sense.

source.place: Monic standard-etale criterion, Tags 00UB, 00UC; pointed universal-cover splitting applied to mu_n

proof.text: Write $r=|I|$ and $f=\prod_i t_i$. For each finite stage $C=C_\lambda$ and $(n,p)=1$ put $K_{\lambda,n}=C[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)$. Repeated monic division gives the basis $x^a$ with $0\le a_i<n$, so this is finite free of positive rank $n^r$ over $C$ and is Noetherian. Its reduction modulo $J$ is $(C/JC)[x_i]/(x_i^n)$. The ideal generated by its $x_i$ is nilpotent (its power $r(n-1)+1$ is zero), and its further quotient is $C/JC$. Idempotents are unchanged by this nilpotent quotient. Since $(C,JC)$ is henselian, idempotents of the finite algebra $K_{\lambda,n}$ are precisely those of $K_{\lambda,n}/JK_{\lambda,n}$, hence those of $C/JC$. The residual finite cover is connected, so $K_{\lambda,n}$ has only $0,1$ as idempotents. It is nonzero by its positive-rank basis, and therefore its spectrum is nonempty connected.

source.place: Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), applied to the finite monic root algebra; Algebra Tag 00J9 (lemma-lift-idempotents)

proof.text:
Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $K_{\lambda,n}$ and let $\mathfrak m$ be its contraction to $C$. Finiteness makes this contraction maximal. Since $JC$ is in the Jacobson radical, $JK_{\lambda,n}$ lies in every maximal ideal as well. Each $x_i^n=t_i$ then forces $x_i\in\mathfrak q$. Set $R=C_\mathfrak m$ and $L=R[x_i]/(x_i^n-t_i)$. By step 6, $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ form an $R$-regular sequence and $R/(t_i)$ is regular local. For $0\le j<r$, substitution gives
$$L/(x_1,\ldots,x_j)\cong (R/(t_1,\ldots,t_j))[x_{j+1},\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)_{i>j}.$$
The remaining monomials are a free basis over $R/(t_1,\ldots,t_j)$. Multiplication by $t_{j+1}$ is injective on every coefficient, hence on this free module. As $x_{j+1}^n=t_{j+1}$, multiplication by $x_{j+1}$ is injective too. The final quotient is $R/(t_i)\ne0$. This proves directly that the $x_i$ form a regular sequence in $L$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, displayed simultaneous parameter-root algebra, printed p.133; agent monomial calculation of its regular sequence

proof.text: Localize the preceding regular sequence at the prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q$. Its entries are in that prime, so it remains a regular sequence in $K_{\lambda,n,\mathfrak q}$. Quotienting by the root coordinates gives the localization of $R/(t_i)$ at its maximal ideal; this is $R/(t_i)$ itself. The identification follows from evaluation $x_i\mapsto0$ and quotient-localization commutation. It is regular local. The regular-sequence lifting theorem therefore makes $K_{\lambda,n,\mathfrak q}$ regular local. Every other prime is contained in a maximal ideal, and localizations of regular local rings are regular. Hence $K_{\lambda,n}$ is regular. Its already proved connectedness and nonemptiness, together with the regular Noetherian normal decomposition, now make $K_{\lambda,n}$ a domain. This argument uses no Noetherianity of $H$.

source.place: Tag 00NU (lemma-regular-mod-x) and Tag 0AFS (lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular)

proof.text: Polynomial presentations commute with the filtered colimit here: assigning the finitely many roots satisfying $x_i^n=t_i$ and a compatible map on all $C_\lambda$ is exactly a map from either $H_n$ or $\varinjlim_\lambda K_{\lambda,n}$. Thus $H_n=\varinjlim_\lambda K_{\lambda,n}$. A filtered colimit of nonzero domains along unital maps is a nonzero domain: if a product is zero, represent its two factors at a common stage and the zero equality at a later stage; one factor is zero there and therefore in the colimit. Also $1=0$ in the colimit would hold at a stage, which is impossible. This proves that $H$, every $H_n$, and $H_\infty$ are nonzero domains. For each $i$, the image of $t_i$ is nonzero at every $C_\lambda$ and $K_{\lambda,n}$: at a maximal ideal it is a nonzerodivisor of the nonzero local ring of $C_\lambda$ (step 6), and the monic basis embeds $C_\lambda$ into $K_{\lambda,n}$. The elementwise colimit criterion therefore keeps every $t_i$, and $f$, nonzero in these colimits.

source.place: Filtered-colimit elementwise criterion (lemma-directed-colimit); agent application to the finite monic root presentations

proof.text: In a nonzero domain the zero ideal is prime and belongs to every nonempty basic open. Thus its spectrum is nonempty irreducible, hence connected. Localizing at a nonzero element is again a nonzero domain: $a/f^b=0$ means $f^ca=0$, hence $a=0$. Apply this to $H,H_n,H_\infty$ and $f$ to get the asserted nonempty connected total and punctured schemes. All are affine (the punctures are principal localizations), so all are qcqs. This also supplies nonemptiness of $U^\circ$, which does not follow merely from nonemptiness of the residual stratum.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, parameter-root chart; agent deduction for its colimit and principal opens

proof.text: After inverting $f$, each $t_i$ and each root $x_i$ is a unit. The monic polynomial $X^n-t_i$ has unit derivative $nX^{n-1}$ in its root quotient. The monic standard-etale criterion, iterated over $i$, shows that $H_n[1/f]$ is etale over $H[1/f]$; composition of etale maps is etale. Its monomial basis has positive rank $n^r$, so every maximal-ideal fibre is a nonzero vector space and the ring map is flat. The flat proper-maximal-ideal criterion makes the map faithfully flat, hence surjective on spectra. It is finite by the same finite basis. Thus every indicated finite punctured level is finite etale and surjective.

source.place: Tags 00UB, 00UC (monic derivative criterion); finite-free basis and faithful flatness criterion

proof.text:
For $n\mid m$, write $d=m/n$. The transition sends $x_{i,n}$ to $x_{i,m}^d$. Elimination of the old root variables gives
$$H_m\cong H_n[y_i]/(y_i^d-x_{i,n})_{i\in I},\qquad y_i\longmapsto x_{i,m}.$$
The inverse sends $x_{i,m}$ to $y_i$; its defining relation is $y_i^m=(y_i^d)^n=t_i$. Repeated monic division gives a positive-rank $d^r$ basis over $H_n$. On the puncture $y_i$ and $d$ are units, so the same derivative calculation proves etaleness of the transition. The same finite-free argument proves surjectivity. These explicit formulas also verify the identity and composite transition laws, since $(x^{m/n})^{n/a}=x^{m/a}$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, power refinements of the parameter-root algebra; agent explicit transition presentation

proof.text: The affine inverse-limit theorem identifies the inverse limit of the punctured finite levels with $\operatorname{Spec}H_\infty[1/f]$: localization commutes with this colimit because compatible maps on either ring are exactly compatible stage maps in which $f$ is a unit. The limit ring is ind-etale over $H[1/f]$, hence weakly etale. The punctured levels are faithfully flat over $H[1/f]$, so their directed colimit is faithfully flat and surjective on spectra. The map is affine, and therefore its single affine source covers the affine target in the fpqc covering condition of the pro-etale site. This proves that $T^\circ\to U^\circ$ is a pro-etale covering, not just a weakly etale map.

source.place: Ind-etale stability and Algebra Tag 090N (lemma-colimit-faithfully-flat); affine inverse limit and the stated pro-etale covering definition

proof.text: For the separate strict-local assertion let $R$ be a strictly henselian regular Noetherian local ring of characteristic $p$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $\kappa$. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ be part of a regular system of parameters, $f=\prod_it_i$, and $(n,p)=1$. Put $K=R[x_i]/(x_i^n-t_i)$. Repeated monic division makes $K$ finite free over $R$ on the monomials $x^a$, $0\le a_i<n$, so $K$ is nonzero, Noetherian, integral over $R$, and $R\to K$ is injective. Since $R$ is henselian, idempotents of the finite algebra $K$ are those of $K/\mathfrak mK=\kappa[x_i]/(x_i^n)$. Its ideal $(x_i)$ is nilpotent with quotient the field $\kappa$, so $K$ has only $0,1$ as idempotents and $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is nonempty connected. Every maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $K$ contracts to $\mathfrak m$ by integrality and contains every $x_i$, since $x_i^n=t_i\in\mathfrak m$. The regular-sequence theorem makes the $t_i$ an $R$-regular sequence with $R/(t_i)$ regular local. Steps 10 and 11 apply verbatim with $C_\mathfrak m$ replaced by $R$ and $L=K$. The $x_i$ form a regular sequence in $K_\mathfrak q$, and $K_\mathfrak q/(x_i)=R/(t_i)$ is regular local. The lifting theorem makes $K_\mathfrak q$ regular local, so $K$ is regular and, being connected, a domain. Each $t_i$ is a nonzerodivisor of the nonzero ring $R$, so $f\neq0$ in $R\subseteq K$. The finite punctured ring $K[1/f]$ is therefore a nonzero domain. The full root ring $\varinjlim_nK_n$ is a nonzero domain by the filtered-colimit argument of step 12, and $f$ stays nonzero at every stage by freeness. Its puncture is consequently a nonzero domain too. Spectra of all these domains are nonempty connected. For $r=0$, $K=R$ is a regular local ring, hence a domain.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, proof, displayed strict-local simultaneous parameter-root algebra $A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)$, printed p.133; agent regularity via the root-coordinate regular sequence of steps 10-11 and Stacks Tag 00NU

proof.text: For the finite chart family chosen in step 2, each $S_U\to S_V$ is the pro-etale covering of step 4. The finite open family $S_V\to S$ covers $S$ and each affine $S_U$ surjects onto $S_V$. The composites are weakly etale by stability under composition. They satisfy the covering condition: over an affine open in $S$, its inverse images in the finitely many $S_V$ are quasi-compact opens of Noetherian affine schemes, so are finite unions of principal opens; pull these back to the corresponding $S_U$ to obtain finitely many affine opens covering that affine target. Thus the composites form a pro-etale covering of $S$. For an empty stratum take the empty family; every requested assertion indexed by a chart is then vacuous.

source.place: Paragraph (3), tame-boundary local calculation; agent assembly of the residual covering family

proof.text: To compare two charts above the same geometric stratum point, take their fibre product over $Y_I$ with the induced point, then an affine neighbourhood of that point. It is etale over either chart by base change, and its reduced stratum is regular. As in step 2, shrink to a nonempty open of its component through the point. It is a chart of the same type. A ring map of these charts preserves the stratum ideals and therefore induces a map on pair henselizations by their universal property. Apply the naturality for pointed scheme morphisms of the universal finite-etale cover to obtain compatible maps on $H$ and on $H/JH$. At finite levels the maps are the maps of pointed finite covers supplied by the equivalence of finite-etale categories. Uniqueness there makes all the diagrams commute before taking colimits. Repeating the fibre-product construction gives common refinements for any finite collection of pointed charts.

source.place: Tag 0A02, universal property of pair henselization; Tag 09ZS, equivalence; naturality of pointed finite-etale covers

proof.text: On such an affine overlap, two equations of the same labelled Cartier ideal differ by a unit: after shrinking, write $t'_i=a_i t_i$ with $a_i$ a unit. For each $(n,p)=1$ the algebra $A[z]/(z^n-a_i)$ is finite etale by monic division and the unit derivative criterion. Choose compatible roots of the fibre value of $a_i$ in $\Omega$ (recursively for prime powers and then for divisibility). The pointed universal-cover splitting gives compatible roots $b_{i,n}$ in $H$ with $b_{i,n}^n=a_i$ and $b_{i,m}^{m/n}=b_{i,n}$. The map between root presentations sends $x'_{i,n}\mapsto b_{i,n}x_{i,n}$; its $n$-th power is $a_it_i=t'_i$. Its compatibility with transitions is the equality $(b_{i,m}x_{i,m})^{m/n}=b_{i,n}x_{i,n}$. On a common refinement of several charts, choose roots for the ratio of each equation to one reference equation, and define the roots of a pairwise ratio by dividing those choices. Their products then give exactly the roots for composed ratios. Naturality of the normalized splitting preserves these prescribed fibre values, so the comparison maps satisfy the cocycle identities. Thus the displayed rings, punctures, and chosen root systems admit the asserted compatible pullbacks on common pointed refinements.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, labelled parameter-root charts; agent comparison by compatible roots of the equation-changing units

proof.text: When $I=\varnothing$, $J=0$ and $f=1$. The pair $(B,0)$ is henselian directly from its idempotent definition, so the pair-henselization universal property identifies $A=B$. There are no root variables or relations, and every $H_n$ and the colimit $H_\infty$ is $H$. Here $S_V=V$ and $U\to V$ is exactly the pointed universal finite-etale limit cover constructed in step 4. All transition and comparison maps reduce to those of that cover. The case $n=1$ for arbitrary $I$ similarly gives $H_1=H$ by substituting $x_i=t_i$.

source.place: Tag 0A02, universal property; agent empty-boundary and exponent-one checks

It is live: not on the side-live route-pivot-dropped list, and its only citer, lem-sfb-tame-root-tower-extension, is live. This is a first split with no re-split repair note. No SGA source is used. I checked ILO IX Prop 2.1 (p.133, the strict-local algebra A[x]/(x_i^n-t_i) with t_i part of a regular system and n prime to char) and VIII Rem 4.2.2(i) against the statement and steps. The STATEMENT-DISPUTED change restricting n to integers prime to p is a genuine correction: for n=p, k[t^±] -> k[x^±] with x^p=t is not etale. The citer uses only (n,p)=1. Dropped cites, repaired: (1) lem-per-ind-etale-regular-coordinate-locus (Steps 1, 6). Step 1 is rebuilt from the SNC dimension formula, 00NR kernel parameters (c=1 for each component, then a comparison in m/m^2 plus Nakayama for the stratum) and the regular-sequence theorem. Step 6 is rebuilt from ind-etale => flat, lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field (092Q; the fibres are reduced and zero-dimensional, so their local rings are fields), lem-weil-pbc-regular-map-ascent (C_lambda regular), flat preservation of the t_i regular sequence, and lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre (031E) for R/(t). (2) lem-per-snc-root-algebra-structure (Step 17, strict-local clause only). Step 17 now applies the item's own Steps 9-11 root-coordinate regular-sequence argument over the henselian local R; roots of unity are not needed, so the lem-sbc-strict-local-roots-of-unity cite is removed too. Steps 10 and 12 now draw their parameter facts from Step 6 (wording only). Batch 5: lem-exc-fields-excellent served only the dropped node's quasi-excellence hypothesis and is removed. lem-exc-regular-local-lift-regular-sequence-quotient (00NU) is kept: its only trf content is the Mathlib Krull-dimension leaf lem-trf-regular-sequence-dimension-formula, which is generic commutative algebra and neither assumed statement nor part of their proofs, so I accept it. The fixed closure has no dropped ids; its remaining trf nodes are generic or already present (the SNC definition and Stacks limit lemmas reached via finite-etale lifting). Artin-Gabber route check: the item is not that node or its children and uses no Qbar, adic, middle t-structure, Gabber finiteness or uniformization, alteration or stable-reduction input. Every other step checked: henselization, finite-etale lifting of the pointed Galois system, idempotents, the Jacobson radical, the monomial regular sequence, colimits of domains, standard etale punctures, faithfully flat colimit cover, the fpqc covering, overlap unit roots and the cocycle, and I empty.
